speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information. To better understand your limp and localized pain, can you tell me exactly where it hurts and if it started after an injury? Also, does the pain get worse when you walk or rest?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; the absence of trauma and fever makes an acute fracture or infection less likely. Does the pain radiate from the hip, or is it strictly localized to the knee joint itself? Also, has this been occurring for more than two weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming the symptoms. Since the pain is localized to the knee but the limp suggests a potential hip issue, can you tell me if you have noticed any stiffness or reduced range of motion when trying to move your left hip? Also, has there been any recent illness, such as a viral infection, in the past few months?

REQUEST TEST: ESR (Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate) and CRP (C-Reactive Protein)
REQUEST TEST: Hip_X-Ray_AAP (Anteroposterior view)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ESR: Normal, CRP: Normal, Hip_X-Ray_AAP: Flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent illness, rash, weight loss, change in appetite or urinary symptoms. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the negative inflammatory markers and X-rays, combined with the classic presentation of a 7-year-old boy with a painful limp and knee pain (referred from the hip), I am ready to provide the final assessment.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE)
